The licensee does not have acquisition records for one adult sulfur-crested cockatoo, three adult budgies, two adult degu,
three adult guinea pigs, one domestic ferret and one hedgehog.
Records containing the required information for animals disposed of, or acquired for, use in regulated activities (including
those offspring born on premises) are necessary to accurately track animals to ensure their humane care and use. The
licensee must make and maintain records of the inventory, acquisition and disposition of all animals which fully and
correctly disclose the required information; these records must be furnished within a reasonable amount of time and as
may be specified in the request for information.
TO BE CORRECTED FROM 07/08/2026 AND GOING FORWARD

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
At the time of inspection, the facility could not produce a completed environmental enhancement plan for avian species
approved by the Attending Veterinarian. The partial plan does not contain adequate descriptions for how the facility
approaches social grouping, environmental enrichment, special considerations, restraint devices and exemptions related
to environmental enhancement for birds. The attending veterinarian has not seen the partial plan.
The Environment Enhancement Plan is required to promote psychological well-being of the avian species at the facility.
The facility must develop, document and follow a species appropriate plan for environmental enhancement adequate to
promote the psychological well-being of birds. The plan must be approved by the attending veterinarian and, at a
minimum, must address social grouping, environmental enrichment, special considerations, restraint, and exemptions to
the plan.
TO BE CORRECTED BY 07/17/2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The enclosure housing an adult male sulfur-crested cockatoo named "Sunny" has an accumulation of urates on the floor
and on enrichment items inside the enclosure.
Accumulations of excreta and other material are porous and can harbor microorganisms that could cause animal illness.
The licensee must ensure that excreta and food waste is removed from primary enclosures and from under and around
primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent excessive accumulation of feces and food waste, to prevent soiling
of the birds and to reduce disease hazards, insects, pests and odors.
TO BE CORRECTED BY 06/26/2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
